params.name: refl
params.let: 'is negative, so the graph is also reflected in the $x$-axis and this point becomes a maximum' if a < 0 else 'is positive, so there is no reflection and this point stays a minimum'

stem: The graph of $y = {=a}\sin\theta {=qs} {=qa}$ is sketched for $0^\circ \le \theta \le 360^\circ$. What is the $y$-value of the turning point at $\theta = 270^\circ$?
solution: On the basic graph $y = \sin\theta$ the turning point at $\theta = 270^\circ$ is the minimum, where $y = -1$.
Multiplying by $a = {=a}$ stretches the graph vertically by a factor of ${=abs(a)}$, and $a$ {=refl}. The point at $\theta = 270^\circ$ therefore moves to $y = {=a} \times (-1) = {=-a}$.
The shift $q = {=q}$ moves every point {=dir} ${=qa}$ units, so $y = {=-a} {=qs} {=qa} = {=q - a}$.
The turning point at $\theta = 270^\circ$ has $y = {=q - a}$.
notes: Standard: read one turning point of y = a sin θ + q from the effects of a (stretch, and reflection when a is negative) and q (shift). Check: a sin 270° + q = q - a, so the answer is q - a for every instance. The sign of a is mixed on purpose so the reflection (the turning point at 270° becomes a maximum) is tested. Zero answers are excluded (q != a). Let-strings contain no backslashes; they use plain words so no escape sequence can be misread.
